content:
Using Signal and hitting the issue of not being able to log in on multiple devices at once? The encrypted messaging service is making it easier for users to use the app across different iPhones and other devices.

Signal users can now link another iPhone to their existing Signal account, rather than being limited to setting up a secondary mobile device as an iPad.

The company also announced Android linking support today, saying: "We're expanding linked devices on iOS so you can link an iPhone to your Signal account, and our support for iPad will continue."

When linking an additional iPhone, users can choose whether to transfer their complete conversation history, as well as media stored within the past 45 days.

Signal says the entire transfer process uses full end-to-end encryption, and employs the same "link-and-sync" technology used for iPad and desktop devices (including the Mac version of the Signal app).

For users who need to use both work and personal iPhones at the same time, or need to test multiple devices simultaneously, this expanded support feature is particularly useful.

This update also brings Signal's multi-device experience closer to Apple's Messages ecosystem, seamlessly syncing conversations across iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

Signal iOS version 8.22 is currently rolling out on the App Store. Signal also recently rolled out a username feature, allowing users to contact each other without sharing phone numbers.
